subject: Civil Engineering
title: Fiber Reinforcement
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fiber Reinforcement usable.

hook.text: Mix tiny steel or plastic fibers into concrete and it resists cracking in every direction.

buildup.text: Steel fibers — short hooked wires — bridge micro-cracks and hold them from spreading.

discovery.text: Polypropylene fibers control plastic shrinkage cracking — the cracks that form before curing.

twist.text: Glass fibers add tensile strength for thin panels — but must resist concrete's alkalinity.

climax.text: Fiber-reinforced concrete lines tunnel walls — no rebar cage needed, faster installation.

punchline.text: Scatter fibers through the mix and cracks have nowhere to grow.

quiz.question: What type of cracking do polypropylene fibers primarily control?
options: Structural cracks caused by heavy loading
Plastic shrinkage cracks that form during early curing before the concrete hardens
Thermal cracks from freeze-thaw cycles in winter
